sentences.text: In Brazil, skipping the vote can cost you your passport.
Who can vote? Voting is a must from 18 to 70. It's optional at 16 and 17, over 70, and if you can't read. Citizens abroad only vote for president.
There's no paper ballot. You type each candidate's number into a machine, check the photo, and press green. Six votes in a row.
Deputies' seats are shared by party votes in each state. So one star candidate can pull others in with them.
That's the 513-member Chamber of Deputies. It makes the laws. The Senate, three per state, must approve them too.
The president runs the government, with no prime minister. If nobody gets over half, the top two meet in a run-off.
In 2026, Lula trailed Flávio Bolsonaro in round one, then won the run-off with 51.8%. But Bolsonaro's party won the most seats in both houses.
So, should anyone be forced to vote?
